cells.title: Judge Windows short-name paths in the mailbox check and fix the union test line endings
cells.judge_obligation_ack: one-character scope change in an existing refusal; the existing read_only_table allow and deny rows pin it
cells.action: Two Windows-only failures from CI run 39916634170. (1) Per D1: in hooks/worker_guard.rs `fn in_mailbox` returns false when `target.contains(['$', '~', '*', '?', '['])`; on Windows the temp path holds an 8.3 short name (`C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...`), so every mv into the mailbox is denied and `hooks::worker_guard::tests::read_only_table` fails. Tilde expansion only happens at the start of a word, so refuse a target that starts with `~` and keep refusing any `$`, `*`, `?` or `[` anywhere. Add rows to `read_only_table` (or a new test beside it): a mailbox path whose directory name holds `~` in the middle (build it with a real temp dir child named like `RUN~1`, created on disk) is allowed for mv into the mailbox, and `mv ~/a <mailbox>/b` is still denied; watch the middle-tilde row fail before the fix. (2) Per D2: in onboard/tests.rs `two_branches_appending_to_the_decision_log_merge_cleanly_after_onboarding` inits a git repo with default settings, and the Windows runner's core.autocrlf turns the merged file into CRLF, so the LF comparison fails. Right after the `init` call add `git_ok(&fx.repo, &["config", "core.autocrlf", "false"]);`. No other changes. No code comments.
cells.verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee worker_guard && PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee two_branches_appending

truths: a mailbox path with ~ in the middle of a directory name is judged by where it points
a path that starts with ~ is still refused
the union-merge test does not depend on core.autocrlf
